根.meaning: A gardening <part>robot</part> tries to pull up a <part>tree</part> to move it, but it won't budge. The robot digs and digs and finds long woody fingers gripping the earth, deeper and deeper, all the way under the house. That's only the first <kanji>root</kanji>.
根.on: A <sound>con</sound>dor swoops down, grabs the robot by its box head and helps it tug.
根.kun: In the end they wrap the roots in a fishing <sound>ne</sound>t and haul the whole tree out together.

材.meaning: A beaver <part>genius</part> gnaws one huge <part>tree</part> into neat square planks in a single night, and by dawn has laid them across the river as a bridge. The other beavers just stare at the stack left over on the bank. That's a lot of <kanji>lumber</kanji>.
材.on: Downstream, his little sister plays a <sound>xy</sound>lophone made of fish bones, not impressed at all.

考.meaning: An old man leans on his <part>cane</part> in front of a <part>stuck javelin</part> that has landed in his vegetable patch. Who threw it? Why? Should he pull it out or leave it? He strokes his beard and takes all afternoon to <kanji>consider</kanji>.
考.on: He thinks so long that the ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne in his other hand melts slowly down to his elbow.
考.kun: Still puzzling, he sniffs a pink <sound>carn</sound>ation and chews a clove of <sound>ga</sound>rlic, which always helps him think.

様.meaning: In a stuffy law office, a <part>sheep</part> clerk hangs her cardigan on a <part>tree</part>-shaped coat stand, dips her <part>fountain</part> pen and writes on every envelope, very slowly, the fussiest title she knows: J. Smith, <kanji>Esq.</kanji>
様.on: Between letters she lets a <sound>yo</sound>-yo roll slowly down and up off the edge of her desk.
様.kun: At lunch she eats one <sound>sa</sound>rdine from a tin and phones her <sound>ma</sound>ma to say how polite she's been.

存.meaning: A <part>child</part> lies in a tiny tent made of <part>one</part> plank, a <part>slash</part> of rope and a <part>pole</part>, staring up at the stars. What if there's a planet made of cake? What if dogs could talk? She lies there and wonders, and starts to <kanji>suppose</kanji>.
存.on: After an hour of supposing she's totally <sound>zon</sound>ked and falls asleep mid-thought.
存.kun: She supposes she'll live to a hundred on warm <sound>na</sound>an and <sound>ga</sound>rlic soup, with a crowd at every birthday shouting '<sound>Rah</sound>!': living on and on.
